tasks.short: Welcome customers and understand what they need.

steps.what: Welcome the customer and establish whether help is wanted.
Ask about intended use, preferences, budget and practical constraints.
Confirm the needs and agree whether to explore suitable merchandise.

tasks.design: Keep the welcome and needs conversation with the salesperson. Configure a short, optional question guide in the {DOCS}, with visual prompts for customers who find open questions difficult.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on timing, trust and interpreting an individual customer's situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document templates can make useful prompts easy to find. No technical breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising hesitation, respecting a wish to browse and discovering needs the customer cannot yet explain.
tasks.human_edge: A salesperson can adjust tone, notice discomfort and build trust without making the interaction feel like a form.
tasks.altitude: The person's week and decision rights remain substantially unchanged. The guide supports less experienced colleagues.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Coach colleagues on welcoming customers during busy periods.
reach.learn: Inclusive questioning, queue triage and observing service without intrusive recording.

evidence.claim: Physical retail greetings and needs discovery commonly depend on interpersonal judgement.
bol Shophulp asks follow-up questions online; this does not demonstrate replacement of an in-store welcome.

assumptions: The baseline is an in-store interaction in a retailer with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Customer needs can remain conversational rather than becoming a stored customer profile.
Time shares are indicative estimates, not measured observations.
No meaningful time saving is assumed.
unknowns: Which languages and accessibility needs are common among customers?
What guidance already exists in the {DOCS}?
Do customers commonly arrive with a saved basket or appointment brief?
research_questions: Which questions help customers explain their needs without making the welcome longer?
Would visual prompts improve understanding for customers who struggle with open questions?
new_work: Maintain the short question guide and visual prompts.
Gather voluntary feedback on whether the prompts help.
tasks.statement: Greet customers and ascertain what each customer wants or needs.

tasks.short: Open and close registers, reconcile takings and prepare cash deposits.

steps.what: Count the opening float and check physical cash custody.
Enter the opening count and open the {OTHER} point-of-sale register.
At closing, count cash and separate charge slips, coupons and vouchers.
Retrieve expected payment totals from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Compare counted amounts with expected totals on the paper cash-up sheet.
Recount discrepancies and investigate missing payment evidence.
Review the reconciliation and approve closing adjustments and the deposit amount.
Retain the next float and seal the approved cash deposit.
Hand over the sealed deposit and retain the deposit receipt.

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} point-of-sale system to collect counts, calculate payment variances and retain closing evidence. Use its existing approval flow, or configure the {WORKFLOW}, to approve adjustments and deposit amounts before passing closing records to the {ERP}. Cash counting, sealing and custody remain physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expected totals may already be automated, while paper cash-up and finance handoffs persist. Physical cash handling cannot be removed by a connector.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing closing functions already calculate expected totals and accept staff counts. Configuration and a small finance connector can remove duplicate calculations and filing.
tasks.still_hard: Someone must count and secure cash, investigate discrepancies and preserve custody. Incorrect counts can make a balanced report misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unexplained variance and take responsibility for cash custody and authorised adjustments.
tasks.altitude: Less closing time goes to calculations and copying figures. Cash custody and adjustment decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Review unresolved closing variances and plan cash-control improvements.
reach.learn: Payment settlement timing, custody evidence and causes of reconciliation differences.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed X-Series closing functions show expected totals by payment type and accept staff-entered counts.
In the Netherlands, employee-data and monitoring arrangements can require works-council consent.
Physical counting and cash custody remain manual in the proposed configuration.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The baseline uses a digital till and paper cash-up sheet, not a spreadsheet.
One person may hold several listed roles; the steps still mark custody and approval changes.
Existing closing functions can replace manual variance calculations.
Deposit handover follows the supervisor's approved instruction; it needs no second software approval.
Access estimates include consultation where employee-linked reporting changes under national rules.
GDPR access and retention controls apply to employee-linked closing records.
Existing cash equipment is retained; no robotics or new surveillance is assumed.
unknowns: Which closing and approval functions are already enabled?
Who counts, approves, seals and deposits cash?
Which evidence is still required on paper?
Are cash-up reports employee-linked, and would their use change?
Does the finance interface support approved closing records and later corrections?
research_questions: Can the existing register enforce a blind count before showing expected cash?
How are late settlements, refunds and deposit receipts linked to the correct closing?
new_work: Review unresolved variances and approve adjustments.
Monitor failed closing transfers to finance.
Maintain payment mappings, approval limits and access permissions.
Check that closing evidence and physical deposit receipts remain traceable.
tasks.statement: Open and close cash registers, performing tasks such as counting money, separating charge slips, coupons, and vouchers, balancing cash drawers, and making deposits.

tasks.short: Stay current on promotions, payment and exchange policies, and security practices.

steps.what: Attend the shift briefing on promotions, policy changes, and security reminders.
Read current notices and check detailed rules relevant to the shift.
Clarify conflicting rules and discuss how to handle unusual situations.
Record completion or acknowledge required updates.

tasks.design: Configure versioned notices in the {DOCS}, filtered by store, role, and effective date, with links to exact changed clauses. Use the {LMS} for required acknowledgements and reminders; the salesperson still confirms completion, and briefings focus on practical questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefings and notices repeat information without reliably showing what changed or when it applies.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioning, audience filters, effective dates, and acknowledgement workflows are standard configuration capabilities. Small connectors are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Reading a notice does not prove understanding. Promotions overlap, and security judgement cannot be reduced to an acknowledgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a rule does not fit the situation and practise a safe response with colleagues.
tasks.altitude: The salesperson spends less time finding current rules and repeating acknowledgements. Policy and security decision rights stay with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Prepare shift briefings around changes that staff must apply.
reach.learn: Check effective dates, distinguish policy from guidance, and use short practical scenarios.

evidence.claim: Versioned notices, targeted distribution, and acknowledgements can be configured without a model loop.
National employee consultation requirements can cover staff-data and monitoring systems; the digest documents Dutch provisions.
The baseline time allocation, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The company already publishes approved notices and uses {LMS} acknowledgements for some required updates.
Acknowledgement means a person's explicit confirmation; opening a notice is not treated as completion.
Only approved text and deterministic change markers are displayed. No model is needed.
GDPR applies to acknowledgement records. National rules determine employee consultation requirements.
Build ranges cover working effort, including access and consultation preparation; formal consultation may take longer.
unknowns: Where are approved notices and policy versions maintained?
Which updates require acknowledgement or demonstrated understanding?
Which national rules and employee representation arrangements apply?
Can existing {DOCS} and {LMS} configuration provide the required filtering?
research_questions: Does showing exact changes improve recall compared with the current briefing?
Which security topics require practical rehearsal rather than reading?
new_work: Assign effective dates and audiences to approved notices.
Retire expired promotions and superseded procedures.
Handle unclear rules and missing acknowledgements.
Maintain retention and access settings for acknowledgement records.
tasks.statement: Maintain knowledge of current sales and promotions, policies regarding payment and exchanges, and security practices.

tasks.short: Calculate purchase totals and accept cash or card payments.

steps.what: Scan merchandise into the checkout system.
Calculate prices, discounts, tax and the purchase total in the checkout system.
Confirm the total, address price queries and ask how the customer will pay.
For cash sales, count tender and return change.
For card sales, enter totals into the payment terminal and obtain authorisation.
Record the settled sale and generate its receipt in the checkout system.
Give the customer their receipt and conclude the transaction.

tasks.design: Configure the checkout system in the {OTHER} to apply price, promotion and tax rules and pass the payable amount to its payment terminal. Keep customer payment authorisation at the terminal and cash handling with the salesperson. Reuse existing sale and receipt recording, adding an {ERP} integration only where duplicate entry remains.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some checkout and payment-terminal combinations require separate amount entry, while accounting interfaces may be incomplete.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing terminal integrations and checkout configuration handle most of the work. AI-assisted coding can make a missing accounting connector cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Cash handling, disputed prices, failed payments and recovery from uncertain payment status remain operational work.
tasks.human_edge: The salesperson resolves awkward payment situations and explains price differences without escalating customer frustration.
tasks.altitude: The person spends less time entering card amounts where this remains manual. Cash handling and exception authority remain unchanged.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Investigate recurring checkout and payment exceptions.
reach.learn: Payment status, duplicate-charge prevention and the difference between pricing errors and settlement errors.

evidence.claim: Checkout systems commonly calculate totals and record sales without a model.
Lightspeed X-Series exposes expected closing totals by payment type; this supports reconciliation, not every proposed transaction interface.
Configured checkout-to-terminal links can remove manual amount entry where compatible interfaces exist.

assumptions: The {OTHER} covers the checkout system and payment terminal.
Cash and card steps are alternative branches; their shares represent average time across the tender mix.
System calculation and recording are already automated and create no new labour saving.
The card step assumes separate terminal entry today; where already integrated, that saving disappears.
A salesperson still supports the customer during card authorisation, although routine terminal entry disappears.
Build ranges cover one supported checkout configuration, with no hardware replacement.
Payment credentials remain within the existing payment service; customer data handling remains subject to GDPR.
Access estimates include a national-rules consultation check if employee-level reporting changes.
unknowns: Are checkout totals already passed directly to payment terminals?
What is the actual cash and card tender mix?
Does the {ERP} already receive sales records without duplicate entry?
Which roles can approve discounts, voids and payment corrections?
How does the checkout system recover after a terminal timeout?
research_questions: Can the existing configuration remove separate amount entry?
Does recovery distinguish an authorised payment from a failed response without charging twice?
How much employee time remains during customer authorisation?
new_work: Maintain price, promotion and tax configurations.
Handle failed, reversed or uncertain payments.
Monitor connector failures and reconcile missing sales records.
Verify terminal behaviour after configuration changes.
tasks.statement: Compute sales prices, total purchases, and receive and process cash or credit payment.

tasks.short: Keep sales records complete, accurate and available for reconciliation.

steps.what: Retrieve daily sales records from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Match paper receipts, vouchers and special-order evidence to recorded sales.
Copy sales figures into the local {SPREADSHEET} sales register.
Compare totals and identify missing or duplicate entries in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Investigate exceptions and confirm authorised corrections in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Archive sales evidence in {DOCS} and send the finance team a summary through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Feed sales events from the {OTHER} point-of-sale system into the {ERP}, using transaction identifiers to prevent duplicates. Deterministic checks link digital evidence in {DOCS} and produce an exception queue, replacing the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register. Staff investigate unresolved evidence and confirm corrections before posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local registers bridge gaps between sales, evidence storage and finance. Different identifiers and paper exceptions make those bridges costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, interfaces and configurable archives cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can make transaction mapping and reconciliation checks cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Paper evidence, offline sales, returns and inconsistent identifiers still need investigation. A matching total alone does not prove completeness.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why a transaction differs and distinguish a genuine correction from an unsupported adjustment.

ambition.what: A receipt-to-sale evidence pack for the finance team.

tasks.altitude: The associate works through evidence exceptions instead of copying sales totals. Correction rights remain within existing limits.

reach.task: Trace special-order deposits, cancellations and fulfilment against sales records.
reach.learn: Transaction identifiers, deposit treatment and order-to-sale status mapping.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed X-Series exposes register closing information and expected payment totals.
Duplicate-safe sales ingestion, evidence linking and completeness checks are deterministic integration patterns; the full proposed design is not a documented case.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The baseline has a digital sales source, a local spreadsheet bridge and some paper evidence.
The prior's large in-person share is not imposed on a predominantly records task.
Evidence with stable digital identifiers is matched automatically; paper exceptions remain manual.
Associates may confirm routine corrections within existing permissions; other adjustments are escalated.
Access and consultation estimates cover employee-linked records under GDPR and applicable national rules.
unknowns: Does a duplicate local register exist, and what purpose does it serve?
Which sales, return and deposit events are available through exports or interfaces?
Which records need statutory retention, and for how long?
Which corrections may associates approve?
Would the proposed reporting change the use of employee data?
research_questions: Can source transaction identifiers survive exports, returns and finance posting?
How will reconciliation detect missing events rather than only mismatched totals?
new_work: Review unmatched evidence and failed imports.
Maintain transaction mappings, access permissions and retention settings.
Check reconciliation coverage after sales or finance system changes.
Escalate corrections beyond the associate's authority.
tasks.statement: Maintain records related to sales.

tasks.short: Notice security risks, respond safely and record incidents.

steps.what: Observe the shop floor and notice possible theft or unsafe situations.
Assess immediate danger and decide whether to alert trained security staff.
De-escalate or handle the incident within training and legal authority.
Write factual observations and the outcome in an incident form in {DOCS}.
Review the incident and assign practical prevention or follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted incident form in {WORKFLOW}, with required factual fields, retention settings and follow-up reminders. Store approved procedures in {DOCS} and show aggregate incident categories in {BI}. Observation, risk assessment and intervention stay with trained people; the design adds no automated suspicion scoring or camera analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recognising danger and responding safely depend on ambiguous physical events. Paperwork can be improved, but that does not solve observation or intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable forms and reminders can reduce reporting effort using existing technology. No model breakthrough is needed for this limited scope.
tasks.still_hard: False accusations, incomplete observations, confrontation and lawful evidence handling remain difficult. Staff must distinguish observed facts from assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: People judge immediate danger, respect dignity and adapt their response to a developing situation.

ambition.what: A weekly review of location-specific security hazards and prevention actions.

tasks.altitude: The week changes little beyond shorter incident paperwork and clearer follow-up. The sales assistant can contribute factual prevention proposals but gains no new authority to search, detain or exclude customers.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Review incident patterns and assign store-layout or staffing remedies.
reach.learn: Use aggregate incident evidence, distinguish correlation from cause, and assess de-escalation options.

evidence.claim: The digest documents false alarms from behaviour-camera deployments, so detection alerts cannot be treated as established theft.
The digest documents an enforcement warning about facial recognition in a Dutch supermarket.
A multi-retailer study documents loss risks associated with self-checkout; automation does not remove security work.
Dutch works-council consent provisions cover certain employee-data and staff-monitoring arrangements; other countries have national rules.
Structured incident forms and reminders can reduce paperwork without automating judgements about people.

assumptions: Trained security support is available directly or through an escalation arrangement.
Observation time is an allocated share of concurrent shop-floor attention, not an additional continuous shift activity.
Incident-response and reporting shares are averaged across routine observation and actual incidents.
The proposed form records necessary factual observations with restricted access and retention under GDPR.
Consultation under national rules is assessed before rollout, especially if incident records could monitor employees.
The estimate covers forms and aggregate reporting; adding surveillance would require a separate assessment and estimate.
unknowns: What security support and escalation arrangements exist?
Which actions are staff trained and authorised to take?
What incident records, retention periods and access controls already exist?
Could the proposed reporting be used to monitor individual employees?
What consultation process and access approvals apply?
research_questions: Which form fields capture useful facts while avoiding unnecessary personal data?
Which aggregate incident categories support practical prevention without identifying staff or customers?
new_work: Maintain incident categories, access permissions and retention settings.
Correct reports that mix observations with unsupported allegations.
Follow up prevention actions and overdue reviews.
Refresh escalation contacts and practical staff training.
tasks.statement: Watch for and recognize security risks and thefts and know how to prevent or handle these situations.

tasks.short: Recommend suitable merchandise and help customers find or obtain it.

steps.what: Search the product catalogue for merchandise matching the customer's needs.

loop.input: A short customer needs brief and permitted catalogue attributes.
loop.output: Structured search criteria and a shortlist of catalogue product identifiers.
loop.check: Validate identifiers and mandatory constraints against catalogue fields; show supporting attributes for each match.
loop.stop: One model pass and one repair attempt, with at most five suggestions; unresolved needs return to manual search.
loop.why_not_simpler: Ordinary filters handle explicit attributes but cannot reliably map all conversational needs to them.

steps.what: Check candidate prices, stock, store locations and fulfilment options.
Explain suitable options and demonstrate the differences that matter to the customer.
Agree the preferred product and any acceptable alternative with the customer.
Guide the customer to the merchandise or retrieve it from the stockroom.

tasks.design: Connect the {ECOMMERCE} catalogue to stock and location data in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, configuring existing filters first. Add a bounded loop only to translate conversational needs into catalogue criteria, then validate price and availability deterministically. The salesperson reviews suggestions before presenting them and handles demonstrations and physical retrieval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product attributes, stock and store locations often sit on separate screens, while customer language does not match catalogue fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search features and interfaces support much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building the connections and a small language interpretation loop.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete specifications, stale stock, subjective preferences and safety-critical suitability still require care.
tasks.human_edge: The salesperson demonstrates products, tests the customer's understanding and judges whether a technically valid option feels right.

ambition.what: Offer a verified in-stock alternative during an out-of-stock conversation.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into repeated searches, leaving more time for demonstrations and comparing alternatives. The salesperson can propose verified alternatives but gains no new pricing or purchasing authority.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Identify recurring gaps between customer needs and the available range.
reach.learn: Product taxonomy, stock availability and how to distinguish a range gap from a temporary shortage.

evidence.claim: bol Shophulp asks follow-up questions and compares product features, price and delivery.
Sponsored products can appear in bol Shophulp, illustrating why recommendation ranking needs explicit commercial rules.
Joining catalogue, price and stock data is deterministic integration work; feasibility depends on available interfaces.

assumptions: The retailer has a searchable catalogue in the {ECOMMERCE} and store stock in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
The solution assists staff; it does not independently contact customers or place orders.
Needs briefs omit customer identity unless it is necessary, with GDPR access and retention controls.
Build ranges are estimates for a limited category pilot with usable interfaces.
Access estimates include consultation screening; applicable national rules may extend the schedule.
unknowns: Are catalogue attributes complete enough to enforce customer constraints?
How current are store stock and shelf locations?
Can existing {ECOMMERCE} configuration already provide the required search?
Which categories require specialist suitability checks?
Would usage records be used for employee monitoring under applicable national rules?
research_questions: How often do configured filters produce a useful shortlist without a model?
Can suggestions remain useful when stock is uncertain or specifications are missing?
Does the shortlist reduce search time while preserving customer satisfaction?
new_work: Review suggested products and handle ambiguous needs.
Correct catalogue attributes and broken stock mappings.
Maintain eligibility and commercial ranking rules.
Sample suggestions for unsupported claims and unsuitable recommendations.
tasks.statement: Recommend, select, and help locate or obtain merchandise based on customer needs and desires.

tasks.short: Answer customer questions about the store and its merchandise.

steps.what: Listen to the question and clarify the customer's situation.
Look up product facts, availability, or store policies.

loop.input: Clarified question, exact product identifiers, current stock record, and approved policy passages.
loop.output: Short answer draft with references and unresolved points.
loop.check: Validate product identifiers, policy dates, prices, and stock deterministically. The salesperson checks cited passages.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one repair pass. Missing or conflicting evidence returns references and an escalation prompt.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact lookups handle structured questions. Varied customer wording and questions spanning several documents need bounded interpretation.

steps.what: Explain the answer and check whether it resolves the question.
Resolve questions requiring an exception or specialist knowledge.

tasks.design: Configure exact lookups across the {ECOMMERCE}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, and approved {DOCS}, then add a bounded drafting loop for questions spanning sources. The salesperson checks references and delivers the answer; exception decisions remain with the retail supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts sit in separate screens, while customer questions rarely use catalogue or policy wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search and data interfaces support exact lookups. AI-assisted coding reduces integration effort, and bounded models can assemble referenced drafts.
tasks.still_hard: Stock freshness, conflicting policies, and identifying the correct product variant. Sensitive exceptions still need a person.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, understand the customer's real concern, and explain uncertainty without making unsupported promises.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer searches and fewer interruptions to colleagues. The salesperson gains time for difficult questions; exception authority does not change.

reach.task: Check availability and delivery status for customer enquiries.
reach.learn: Read stock reservations, delivery statuses, and the limits of availability promises.

evidence.claim: Retail assistance can interpret customer questions and compare merchandise attributes and delivery information.
Fixed flows plus FAQ retrieval have supported retail service enquiries in a documented deployment.
The proposed internal assistant, time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The baseline is an assisted store sale, with most conversation happening face to face.
The stock record is in {OPS_SYSTEM}; a till or product-information system would use {OTHER} if appropriate.
Drafts remain internal. Human review time is included in lookup effort; the salesperson delivers the external answer.
GDPR applies to customer information. Access work includes retention choices and consultation under national rules where applicable.
Build ranges estimate working effort for a narrow pilot with existing interfaces, not elapsed approval time.
unknowns: Which systems contain authoritative product, stock, and policy information?
What interfaces and permissions are available?
Which question categories require supervisor approval?
How much lookup time and escalation effort occurs today?
research_questions: What proportion of real questions can exact lookup or fixed answers resolve?
Can referenced drafts preserve the correct product variant and all material policy qualifications?
new_work: Review references before using drafts.
Route missing or conflicting answers to source owners.
Maintain source versions, access controls, and interface mappings.
Sample incorrect answers without creating individual staff performance scores.
tasks.statement: Answer questions regarding the store and its merchandise.

tasks.short: Explain merchandise features, use, operation, and care to customers.

steps.what: Identify the product and what the customer needs to understand.
Check specifications, operating instructions, and care guidance for the exact product.
Explain relevant features, operating steps, care requirements, and limitations.
Check understanding and point out instructions the customer can consult later.

tasks.design: Configure exact product lookup in the {DOCS} and use a deterministic template to assemble product-specific care cards from approved passages. The salesperson checks the selected instructions, explains them, and offers a printed card or public link for later reference.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions are spread across manuals and leaflets, with inconsistent product identifiers. Preparing a concise handout takes extra effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable product identifiers, document indexing, and template assembly support a small deterministic tool. AI-assisted coding can speed up the document mappings.
tasks.still_hard: Source documents may omit practical details or contain conflicting versions. The salesperson must judge whether the customer understands safety-critical instructions.
tasks.human_edge: Relate instructions to the customer's situation and recognise when explanation or specialist advice is still needed.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into finding instructions and preparing follow-up material. The salesperson can offer a reusable care card within approved guidance; technical and safety policy authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a clear product-use handout for a demonstration.
reach.learn: Select approved passages, preserve warnings, and check that the handout matches the exact model.

evidence.claim: Template assembly can produce care cards from approved product passages without generating new technical advice.
Retail assistance depends on the quality of seller product data.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are estimates for the proposed design.

assumptions: This task covers verbal explanation; physical demonstration is accounted for separately.
The pilot uses approved passages that can be selected by product and topic without rewriting.
Care cards retain applicable warnings and link to full instructions.
The salesperson checks the card before handing it to the customer; this is part of the manual external action.
Public instruction links avoid collecting customer contact details. GDPR applies if identifiable delivery records are added.
Build ranges estimate working effort for one product category with available source documents.
unknowns: Are manuals current, reusable, and mapped to exact product variants?
Which care topics need specialist approval?
Can approved passages be reused without losing essential context?
Would customers prefer printed cards or public links?
research_questions: Does a care card improve customer understanding and later recall?
Can deterministic passage selection preserve every applicable warning across product variants?
new_work: Approve reusable care passages and maintain product mappings.
Check cards when manuals or product variants change.
Handle questions that approved instructions do not answer.
Remove outdated cards and repair broken public links.
tasks.statement: Describe merchandise and explain use, operation, and care of merchandise to customers.

tasks.short: Prepare price tickets and arrange merchandise into attractive, accessible displays.

steps.what: Read the display brief and promotion dates in {DOCS}.
Generate price tickets in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system.
Choose merchandise and adapt the display layout to available space.
Move merchandise, attach tickets and arrange the display.
Check ticket accuracy, visibility, stability and customer access before opening the display.

tasks.design: Configure {WORKFLOW} to turn promotion dates and approved briefs from {DOCS} into a dated display checklist. Configure the {OTHER} point-of-sale system to generate tickets from current prices; the sales assistant adapts the layout, installs the display and checks it before customers use it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Much of the task is physical. Briefs, promotion dates and ticket printing can also sit in separate places.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, scheduling and price exports can handle preparation. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting them; it does not move merchandise.
tasks.still_hard: Space constraints, unstable items, missing stock and visual balance need attention on the shop floor.
tasks.human_edge: The sales assistant sees how customers move, notices awkward displays and makes practical aesthetic choices.

ambition.what: A weekly display adjustment based on aggregate product sell-through.

tasks.altitude: The week remains mostly physical display work, with less ticket preparation. The sales assistant can propose local layout changes; pricing and promotion authority do not change.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Evaluate display performance and plan the next display change.
reach.learn: Read aggregate sell-through, distinguish stock shortages from weak presentation, and compare similar trading periods.

evidence.claim: Ticket templates and scheduled display checklists are feasible deterministic preparation aids; physical arrangement remains human.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: A central merchandising team supplies approved briefs and prices.
The {OTHER} point-of-sale system supports ticket templates or a usable price export.
Preparation occupies a small share of this task; the predominantly physical prior is retained.
The access estimate covers a shared checklist without individual performance tracking. National rules may require consultation if the scope changes.
Build ranges describe a small pilot, not a rollout across all stores.
unknowns: Which ticket formats and price-export interfaces are available?
Who may approve local display changes?
How often do promotion dates or printed prices conflict?
What access and consultation procedures apply?
research_questions: Can existing ticket configuration cover the required formats without custom code?
Which aggregate sales comparison would help staff assess display changes fairly?
new_work: Maintain ticket templates and promotion schedules.
Resolve missing prices and conflicting promotion dates.
Check that automated checklists reflect actual store space.
tasks.statement: Ticket, arrange, and display merchandise to promote sales.

tasks.short: Prepare sales slips and contracts from agreed purchases.

steps.what: Confirm purchased items, customer details and agreed terms.
Enter or scan purchase details into the point-of-sale system.
Generate a sales slip or populate a contract template.
Check amounts and terms; approve contract release or escalate exceptions.
Present contracts for customer acceptance and collect required signatures.
Give the customer a copy and file the sales document.

tasks.design: Configure the point-of-sale system in {OTHER} to reuse purchase details, then generate approved templates from {DOCS} with deterministic code. Route contract exceptions through {WORKFLOW}, collect required acceptance through {ESIGN}, and file and deliver copies through {DOCS} and {EMAIL}; routine slips use existing issuance rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Purchase data and contract templates often sit apart. Bespoke terms and signatures have kept manual copying in the process.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template, signature and integration capabilities cover most of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining mapping and validation.
tasks.still_hard: Template versioning, delivery commitments and nonstandard terms need clear ownership. GDPR applies to customer data; consumer-contract requirements and employee consultation depend partly on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Explain obligations clearly, spot misunderstood terms and negotiate exceptions within delegated authority.

ambition.what: Remote customers who need signed sales contracts

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into copying details and filing documents; more goes into explaining unusual terms. Pricing and legal approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Validate order completeness before fulfilment.
reach.learn: Required order fields, delivery dependencies and amendment controls.

evidence.claim: Structured sales data can populate approved document templates without a model loop.
Electronic signature and filing workflows can reduce contract administration while preserving customer acceptance.

assumptions: This is a mixed retail setting with routine slips and some higher-value contracts.
Routine slips skip the signature step; the time split represents the combined task.
The point-of-sale system is represented by {OTHER}.
Existing automatic receipt generation offers little additional saving; gains mainly concern contracts and duplicate entry.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
unknowns: The proportion of slips versus contracts and existing template automation.
Available interfaces, signature capabilities and document retention rules.
Which terms require supervisor approval.
Applicable national consultation requirements and internal access lead times.
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove duplicate entry before custom code is built?
Which contract fields cause corrections after customer acceptance?
new_work: Maintain approved templates, field mappings and validation rules.
Review nonstandard terms and failed document deliveries.
Monitor signature completion and reconcile missing filed copies.
tasks.statement: Prepare sales slips or sales contracts.

tasks.short: Find unavailable merchandise and arrange a store transfer or special order.

steps.what: Clarify the customer's item, acceptable alternatives, budget and delivery needs.
Search the {OPS_SYSTEM} for stock at other locations.
Call another store or supplier to confirm availability and delivery.
Explain price and timing, then obtain the customer's choice.
Enter and submit the agreed order in the {OPS_SYSTEM} or {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Send the customer an order confirmation and later delivery updates through {EMAIL}.

reach.task: Check whether a proposed material meets the customer's application requirements.
reach.learn: Coverage conditions, substrate compatibility and the limits of manufacturer specifications.

reach.task: Convert a quantity estimate into orderable packs and accessories.
reach.learn: Pack rounding, batch availability and required companion items.

evidence.claim: Area, coverage, pack rounding and price calculations can use deterministic rules once inputs are confirmed.
A bounded extraction loop can propose specification fields with source passages for human checking.
The digest provides no documented case for this project-estimation workflow or its projected time savings.

assumptions: This describes a project-based retailer selling products such as paint or flooring.
A {SPREADSHEET} calculation is a typical bridge here; retailers with an existing estimator should configure it first.
The situational-input prior remains valid. Once measurements and material assumptions are confirmed, arithmetic has higher rule coverage.
The physical customer conversation is preserved; the main reduction comes from calculation and quote preparation.
The starter covers one material family. Further families require separate rules and verification.
Employee review time includes checking extracted parameters; customers' measurement work is outside the time shares.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply where customer information or model processing is involved. National rules determine any consultation.
Build ranges are planning estimates for a reusable starter, including access and consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which product families, units and waste rules are used?
Does an existing estimator already handle these calculations?
Are specifications available as structured fields or only documents?
Who verifies customer measurements and approves material suitability?
Which quotes are indicative and which create a binding commitment?
Can current prices and stock be accessed through approved exports or interfaces?
research_questions: Which material families can share calculation rules without hiding important differences?
How accurately can extraction recover coverage conditions as well as numeric coverage values?
Which historical estimate errors came from arithmetic rather than incorrect project assumptions?
new_work: Approve new or changed specification parameters.
Maintain material rules, units and pack sizes.
Handle missing measurements and conflicting specifications.
Check calculator changes against representative projects.
Retire stale specification versions and price feeds.
tasks.statement: Estimate quantity and cost of merchandise required, such as paint or floor covering.

tasks.short: Rent merchandise, explain its use, and record handover and return.

steps.what: Discuss the intended use, rental period and customer's experience.
Check rental records in {OTHER} for availability, rates and item history.
Select a suitable item and inspect its condition and accessories.
Prepare rental terms, explain charges and obtain the customer's agreement.
Take the rental payment or deposit through the till system in {OTHER}.
Demonstrate safe use, confirm understanding and hand over the item.
Update rental records in {OTHER} with the item, customer and return deadline.
Inspect the returned item, check accessories and discuss reported faults.
Close the rental in {OTHER}, settle charges and release any remaining deposit.

tasks.design: Configure rental records in the {OTHER} rental system for availability, agreements, item identifiers and barcode handover and return events. Connect the {OTHER} till system where supported so payment status and approved settlements update the rental record without re-entry. The salesperson retains suitability checks, demonstrations, condition inspections and approval of customer charges.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rental records, till payments and physical condition checks are separate. Some retailers have only partly configured their existing rental software.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rental software already supports availability, item history and barcode events. A small connector can remove repeated payment and status entry.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, customer competence and disputed damage remain human work. Concurrent bookings and deposit handling require reliable transaction controls.
tasks.human_edge: Judge suitability, demonstrate safe use and resolve disagreement about returned condition.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less record entry and more time for demonstrations and difficult returns. Decision rights remain unchanged, including approval limits for charges and deposit releases.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of retail sales workers
reach.task: Resolve disputed damage charges and unavailable-item substitutions.
reach.learn: Condition evidence, charging limits and maintenance quarantine rules.

reach.task: Teach customers how to operate unfamiliar rental equipment.
reach.learn: Demonstration structure and practical checks of customer understanding.

evidence.claim: Booqable supports rental availability, item rental history and barcode check-in.
Payment and rental status synchronization depends on the interfaces available in the installed systems.
Physical demonstrations and condition inspections limit how much of the whole task can be automated.

assumptions: The retailer operates a rental counter with existing rental records; {OTHER} covers both rental and till systems as separate categories.
Time shares cover one completed rental lifecycle, including return, and exclude elapsed rental time.
The communication-heavy prior is retained, but availability lookup and records have stronger rule coverage.
Payment automation prepares amounts and updates records; the salesperson approves collection and settlement.
Returned items become available only after a satisfactory inspection. Failed items enter maintenance quarantine.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine retention, consumer terms and any employee consultation.
Build ranges cover configuration and one payment connection, including access and consultation where required.
unknowns: Which rental and till features are already licensed and configured?
Can item identifiers and payment references be shared between systems?
How are reservations protected against concurrent bookings?
Which rentals require identity checks, competence checks or special instructions?
Who may approve damage charges, refunds and deposit releases?
How are cleaning, inspection and maintenance delays reflected in availability?
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove re-entry without adding a separate records app?
Which payment interface supports the retailer's actual deposit and refund process?
Which return events must keep an item unavailable until further inspection?
new_work: Resolve payment synchronization failures and duplicate booking events.
Maintain rental rates, agreement templates and item identifiers.
Review proposed settlements and escalate disputed damage.
Correct missing handover or return events.
Maintain inspection and quarantine statuses.
tasks.statement: Rent merchandise to customers.

role_batches.altitude: The role remains centred on customers and physical merchandise. Better product lookup and connected checkout records reduce some screen work, while advice, payment exceptions and readiness decisions retain their existing human authority.
reach: Support the first-line supervisor of retail sales workers with recurring range gaps and checkout exceptions.
Help order clerks resolve preparation delays using clear item and readiness records.
skills_to_grow: Needs discovery and accessible product explanation.
Checking product claims against catalogue facts.
Recognising uncertain stock and payment status.
Recording useful exceptions without unnecessary personal data.
Maintaining practical preparation checklists.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a stronger cross-category adviser who can quickly assemble verified alternatives and explain their trade-offs, while retaining hands-on responsibility for customer service and merchandise.

role_batches.altitude: Retail sales remains a customer-facing job. Faster reference lookup and simpler preparation leave more attention for explanation, supervised trials, and difficult questions; pricing, policy, and safety exception rights stay with authorised roles.
reach: Order clerk: interpret availability and delivery statuses before making customer promises.
Retail supervisor: turn current policy changes into practical briefing questions.
Product promoter: prepare demonstrations and approved product-care handouts.
skills_to_grow: Match exact product variants to authoritative instructions.
Check references, effective dates, and stock freshness.
Explain limitations clearly and confirm customer understanding.
Recognise when a question needs supervisor or specialist judgement.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a stronger product adviser who combines reliable reference tools with hands-on teaching and product-specific take-home care guidance.

role_batches.altitude: The role remains centred on customers and physical merchandise. Less preparation and transaction entry create room for stock exceptions, difficult returns and small display improvements; financial and security authority remain within existing limits.
reach: Support the retail supervisor's stockout and display reviews using aggregate sales and stock evidence.
Help order clerks resolve purchase traces, supplier acknowledgements and return transaction mismatches.
Contribute factual incident patterns to the retail supervisor's prevention planning.
skills_to_grow: Stock reconciliation, lead times and replenishment economics.
Consumer remedies under national rules and clear explanations of return decisions.
Aggregate sales analysis and practical display evaluation.
De-escalation, factual incident reporting and careful handling of personal data.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A sales assistant who combines customer service with a regular improvement brief: identify a stockout risk, test a display change, resolve a recurring return problem and propose a practical safety improvement.

role_batches.altitude: The largest gains come from connected stock information and removing duplicate sales administration. Customer conversations, cleaning and cash custody remain substantial parts of the week; new commercial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Order clerk: trace special orders, deposits and delivery exceptions.
Retail supervisor: interpret closing exceptions and improve cash-control routines.
skills_to_grow: Read stock availability and reservation states.
Trace sales, deposits and returns through shared identifiers.
Investigate reconciliation exceptions using source evidence.
Explain uncertain fulfilment options to customers.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a store fulfilment specialist who resolves difficult availability requests and follows delayed orders through to delivery, within agreed reservation and spending limits.

role_batches.altitude: Sales paperwork and valuation preparation shrink; physical service and commercial judgement remain central. Approval limits stay unchanged, while better records support informed discussions about trade-in margins.
reach: Order clerk: check sales records for fulfilment completeness.
Sales manager: compare trade-in allowances with realised margins.
Retail supervisor: improve packing-station layout and material replenishment.
Demonstrator and product promoter: explain fit-related features through clear demonstrations.
skills_to_grow: Recognise contract exceptions and explain terms clearly.
Interpret valuation evidence and resale margins.
Maintain accurate product, size and condition records.
Provide respectful fitting assistance and accessible demonstrations.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A salesperson who supports remote contract completion and brings evidence to trade-in pricing discussions, while retaining skilled, personal service at the counter.

role_batches.altitude: Retail salespeople spend less time transferring data and preparing documents, while retaining customer conversations and physical checks. They can present priced alternatives sooner; financial, technical and commercial decision rights expand only through explicit delegation.
reach: Order clerk: prepare complete orders and resolve fulfillment exceptions.
First-line supervisor of retail sales workers: assess disputed charges and nonstandard quotes.
Sales manager: compare bundle margins and commercial outcomes.
Demonstrator and product promoter: teach safe use and check customer understanding.
skills_to_grow: Validate measurements, units, prices and source versions.
Explain estimates, exclusions and contractual commitments plainly.
Use structured forms without losing important customer context.
Recognize when technical or financial judgement requires another qualified role.
Diagnose failed handoffs and distinguish drafts from approved commitments.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a project adviser who presents priced purchase, rental, repair and replacement options using reusable calculators and approved data. Start with portable forms and templates; connect company systems as access permits, while keeping diagnosis and regulated decisions with authorized roles.
